result.title: Preface
result.summary: The City of Austin Employees’ Retirement System (COAERS) issued a June 26, 2025 RFP for actuarial services for its defined benefit plan using an Actuarially Determined Contribution (ADC) rate. Key dates: questions due July 16; pre-proposal conference July 24; proposals due July 30; bid opening July 31; finalist review November 13, 2025 (time TBD). Inquiries and proposals go to rfp@coaers.org; contact Russell Nash, Deputy Executive Director. The RFP covers COAERS’ funding approach, ADC and contribution corridors, liability schedules, investments, experience studies, and assumptions; core services including annual valuations, GASB reporting, QEBA allocation, member-account interest recommendations, financial-statement assistance, studies, and deadlines; and contract terms, including performance, termination, confidentiality, insurance, liability, records, audits, conflicts, and legal requirements. It also sets proposal schedules, registration, submission and format rules, evaluation and selection procedures, and includes submission, conflict, contact, trade-secret, staff, firm, scope, cost, and proposal-format exhibits and a checklist.

result.summary: COAERS seeks proposals from qualified firms adhering to the American Academy of Actuaries’ Code of Professional Conduct for full-scope actuarial services. The intended agreement is a five-year Master Services Agreement covering calendar years 2026–2030, with annual engagement letters due by October 1 before each year. RFP materials—including registration, actuarial reports and data, policies, sample letters/reports, funding information, and statutes—are available at coaers.org/RFP. Questions are due to Russell Nash at rfp@coaers.org by 5 p.m. Central July 16, 2025; written responses follow the optional virtual pre-proposal conference at noon July 24. Proposals are due by 5 p.m. July 30; a virtual public bid opening is July 31 at noon, when firm names will be read. Selected respondents may be asked to give a no-cost, approximately 90-minute presentation in Austin. Until selection, respondents may contact only the designated email, not listed Board members, except through Board/Committee meetings or existing business relationships; violations may disqualify firms.

result.title: ADMINISTRATIVE MATTERS
result.summary: COAERS is a single-employer governmental defined-benefit retirement system established by City ordinance in 1941, governed by Texas law since 1991, and qualified under IRC Section 401(a). Its 11-member Board oversees operations for members and beneficiaries. Participating employers are the City of Austin (over 17,000 active/deferred members and 7,100 retirees) and COAERS staff (38 active/deferred members and 13 retirees). The Board selects the actuary, who values assets and liabilities and calculates employer contributions under Texas Civil Statutes Article 6243n; the Benefits and Services Committee oversees valuations and studies. COAERS staff and its audit and investment consultants support administration; the City administers OPEB. The calendar-year ACFR includes financial statements, management discussion, schedules, and actuarial studies and reports, including GASB 67; the actuary also prepares the City’s GASB 68 report. COAERS has no component units and belongs to no other reporting entity. Its office is at 4700 Mueller Boulevard, Austin. Microsoft Dynamics GP supports accounting and reporting; PensionGold 3 manages pension records, claims, and payroll.

result.title: SECTION ONE - FUNDING APPROACH
result.summary: COAERS funds long-term pension obligations through an actuarially determined contribution (ADC): Entry Age Normal normal cost, a 0.70%-of-pay administrative expense assumption, and amortized gain/loss layers, less employee contributions, determine the employer rate. Annual valuations and Risk Sharing Valuation Studies guide rates; a corridor has minimum, midpoint, and maximum rates 5% of pay apart. If the ADC exceeds the maximum, employee contributions may rise from 10% by up to 2%; further shortfalls prompt funding discussions. Below the midpoint with funding under 90%, the employer rate remains at the midpoint. For 2024–2026, minimum/midpoint/maximum rates are 3.68/8.68/13.68%, 2.44/7.44/12.44%, and 2.21/7.21/12.21%; ADCs are 8.68%, 8.47%, and 10.05%. The section covers corridor projections through 2053, post-2022 amortization layers, and the City’s separate Legacy Liability payment schedule. It describes $3.5 billion in investments, allocation and oversight, five-year experience studies, and 2024 assumptions: 2.5% inflation, 6.75% return, 1.25% wage inflation, 3.75% ultimate salary scale, 3.5% payroll growth, and specified mortality assumptions.

nodes.title: 1.1 Funding Approach in General
nodes.summary: COAERS uses an actuarially determined contribution (ADC) approach: the actuary calculates normal cost as a percentage of pay, including administrative expenses and post-2022 gain/loss amortization layers, forecasts the next year’s cost, and subtracts employee contributions to determine the employer rate. Employers must also make scheduled Legacy Liability payments to retire the UAAL. The funding objective is to meet long-term pension obligations. Policies include paying off the UAAL over a closed 30-year period; conducting annual actuarial valuations, including Risk Sharing Valuation Studies, to set upcoming employer rates; monitoring rates against a corridor midpoint; increasing employee contributions, up to a 2% maximum, if the employer ADC exceeds the midpoint by more than 5% of pay, and discussing plan changes if employer and employee maximums are exceeded; and conducting experience studies at least every five years to review assumptions and methods. The latest study was as of December 31, 2024.

nodes.title: 1.2 Actuarial Determined Contribution
nodes.summary: COAERS uses an actuarially determined contribution (ADC), consisting of normal cost, a 0.70%-of-pay administrative expense assumption, and amortized liability layers for actuarial gains or losses. Normal cost for each benefit component is calculated using the Entry Age Normal method. Liability layers established for 2023 and 2024 will continue to be calculated annually: losses increase the contribution and gains reduce it. The actuary projects the coming year’s normal cost and subtracts the employee contribution to determine the employer rate. A Risk Sharing Valuation Study as of December 31, 2022 set a contribution corridor with a midpoint based on the expected employer-rate trajectory and minimum and maximum rates 5% of pay below and above it. If the ADC exceeds the maximum, employee contributions must rise from the current 10%, by up to 2% of payroll. If that is insufficient, COAERS and Austin must discuss a funding and expense plan. If the ADC falls below the midpoint while the funded ratio is under 90%, the employer rate stays at the midpoint.

nodes.title: 1.3 Contribution Rate Corridor & ADC 2024 - 2026
nodes.summary: The text presents the 2024–2026 contribution rate corridors: minimums of 3.68%, 2.44%, and 2.21%; midpoints of 8.68%, 7.44%, and 7.21%; maximums of 13.68%, 12.44%, and 12.21%; and ADC rates of 8.68%, 8.47%, and 10.05%, respectively. It also references corridor midpoint, maximum, and minimum projections through 2053. Gains and losses after 2022 create new normal-cost amortization layers, initially using the Legacy Liability’s remaining period; once that period falls below 20 years, new layers use a closed 20-year period. A 2022 actuarial valuation established additional annual City payments to retire the unfunded liability; the full schedule is available at coaers.org/RFP. As of March 31, 2025, COAERS investments totaled $3.5 billion. The Board adopted a diversified, long-term, risk-adjusted strategic allocation, with private-market investments expected to take time to reach target levels.

The RSVS performed as of December 31, 2022 created a Legacy Liability amortization schedule which establishes the payments the City of Austin is to contribute in addition to the ADC each year to retire the unfunded actuarial accrued liability. nodes.summary: As of March 31, 2025, COAERS held $3.5 billion in investments. The Board adopted a diversified strategic asset allocation across global equities, private equity, real assets, private credit, fixed income, and cash, designed to support strong long-term, risk-adjusted returns; implementing the private-market components will take time. Investments are managed prudently and solely to provide member and beneficiary benefits and pay reasonable administrative expenses. The Board’s Investment Policy Statement and guidelines govern the program, supported by an Investment Committee that researches, recommends, and monitors portfolio matters. Meketa Investment Group provides investment consulting, while four COAERS professionals oversee daily implementation.

nodes.title: 1.8 Experience Studies
nodes.summary:
1.8 Experience Studies
COAERS believes that a periodic review of our actuarial assumptions is crucial to understanding and managing the cost of the benefits promised to members of COAERS. The use of outdated or inappropriate assumptions can result in understated costs which will lead to higher future contribution rates; or overstated costs which place an unnecessary financial burden on the City of Austin and its employees. Accordingly, COAERS conducts experience studies every five years. During each experience study, each assumption is reviewed and compared to the actual experience of the plan with consideration of adding in a slight margin for adverse experience. Then the assumptions, as a whole, are reviewed for reasonableness and consistency. COAERS recently reviewed its actuarial assumptions based on census data as of December 31, 2024. Certain key assumptions are listed below. A full discussion of the assumptions can be found in the Experience Study Report at www.coaers/RFP.

result.title: SECTION TWO – CORE SCOPE OF SERVICES
result.summary: Respondents must quote an annual fixed price for core services over the five-year term; other work is priced through annual engagement letters. Services require direct supervision and approval by an identified actuary with at least 10 years’ experience and qualifying SOA/AAA credentials. Annual work includes valuations using specified cost, asset-smoothing, and amortization methods; a Risk Sharing Valuation Study; secure census-data review and reconciliation; required actuarial/GASB tables and reporting; one Austin committee presentation; requested IRC §415(b)/QEBA calculations (up to 50 people over the term); and a Board interest-crediting-rate recommendation. The contractor also provides the auditor an annual investment-assumption memo and independence letter, conducts an experience study by 2029 with recommendations and implementation support for specified benefit calculations, and assists with an asset/liability study before 2030. Deadlines are specified for annual and periodic deliverables, presentations, and reports, generally by 5 p.m. Central on the last business day of the designated week; asset/liability assistance timing is to be determined.

nodes.title: 2.1 Personnel
nodes.summary:
SECTION TWO – CORE SCOPE OF SERVICES
Respondents will use Exhibit H to provide an annual fixed price for the core scope of services as described in this section for each year of the five-year term. All other services provided will be priced as agreed to by COAERS by an annual Engagement Letter at the time of the request during the contract.
2.1 Personnel
All services provided for the scope of services described herein must be performed under the direct supervision of a Supervising Actuary who have been regularly engaged in the business of providing actuarial services for at least 10 years and must have the designation of either an Associate or Fellow of the Society of Actuaries and/or Member of the American Academy of Actuaries. The Supervising Actuary must approve all the work provided to COAERS. The Respondent will identify the Supervising Actuary in its response.

nodes.title: 2.2 Annual Actuarial Valuation (Including a Risk Sharing Valuation Study)
key_items: SECTION TWO – CORE SCOPE OF SERVICES
nodes.summary: The annual actuarial valuation uses Entry Age Normal cost, five-year asset smoothing (recognizing 20% of investment gains/losses annually, with offsetting unrecognized amounts immediately recognized), and declining 30-year amortization to 20 years, then closed 20-year layers. Funding period is the weighted average of layers; negative amortization is to be eliminated as soon as possible but is expected until the legacy liability schedule reaches 20 years. The Risk Sharing Valuation Study includes an executive summary and discussion of contribution corridors and rates, legacy liabilities/payments, gain/loss layers, funded status, asset changes, actuarial gains/losses, risk disclosures, methods and assumptions, tables, definitions, and applicable actuarial/GASB requirements. The contractor securely receives, reviews, tests, reconciles, and discloses census-data issues and provides one annual in-person Austin presentation. Annual GASB 67 plan schedules and GASB 68 City financial information are due April 15; neither requires a presentation. On request, QEBA calculations determine IRC §415(b) limits and benefit allocations, estimated for up to 50 people over the contract. Each year, the contractor recommends member-account interest rates to the Board in a letter.

Annual GASB 67 plan reporting schedules and GASB 68 financial reporting information for the City of Austin, meeting Attachment 2 minimum content, are due by April 15; neither requires a presentation. Upon request, the contractor will calculate IRC §415(b) limits and allocate annuitant benefits between the Plan Trust and QEBA, for an estimated maximum of 50 people over the contract (currently 13); no presentation is required.

nodes.summary: The contractor will annually recommend an interest crediting rate to the Board of Trustees using Attachment 12, Board Policy I-3, with no travel or presentation. Annually, it will provide COAERS’ financial statement auditor an investment-return-assumption reasonableness memo and a letter certifying specified information and describing the contractor’s independence; no travel or presentation is required. By December 31, 2029, at least once, it will conduct an experience study of current assumptions and methods against recent experience, recommend appropriate changes, and report findings and methodological recommendations in accordance with accepted actuarial principles and applicable standards. It will assess administrative impacts and provide implementation information, calculations, or actuarial-equivalence approaches for specified service-purchase, lump-sum, retirement-factor, tax-limit, and returned-to-work benefit calculations. It must travel to Austin for separate presentations to the Benefits & Services Committee and full Board. Before December 31, 2030, it will at least once assist the investment consultant with an asset/liability study by supplying projections of assets, liabilities, funded status, benefit payments, and liquidity needs; no travel or presentation is required.

nodes.title: Actuarial Assistance and Experience Studies
nodes.summary: The contractor will use COAERS’ Board-approved Interest Allocation Determination policy to recommend an interest rate; no travel or formal presentation is required for this work. Annually, it will provide the financial statement auditor an investment return assumption reasonableness memo and a letter certifying specified information and describing independence from COAERS; no travel or presentation is required. At least once by December 31, 2029, it will conduct an experience study reviewing actuarial assumptions and methods against recent experience, recommending appropriate changes under accepted actuarial principles and Actuarial Standards of Practice. A report will present findings and recommendations for each assumption and actuarial methods. The contractor will assess administrative impacts and provide implementation information, calculations, or actuarial-equivalence approaches for service purchases, partial lump sums, early retirement reductions, joint-and-survivor annuities, IRC Section 415 limits, and benefit recalculations for retirees returning to work. It will travel to Austin twice to present to the Benefits & Services Committee and Board of Trustees.

nodes.title: 2.10 Performance Standards - Deadlines for the Completion of Core Services
nodes.summary: Section 2.10 sets performance deadlines for annual and periodic deliverables, all due by 5 p.m. Central on the last business day of the stated week. Annual deadlines: COAERS actuarial census data—first week of January; respondent questions/reconciling items—third week of January; QEBA allocation—second week of January; COAERS year-end financial statements—first week of February; actuarial valuation services, including the risk-sharing study—fourth week of February; committee PowerPoint—first week of March; in-person Benefits & Services Committee presentation in Austin—second week of April; final risk-sharing study—first week of April; financial-statement actuarial assistance, GASB 67 reporting/accounting information, and GASB 68 information for the City of Austin—second week of April; interest-rate recommendation letter for member accounts—first week of December. Periodic Experience Study deadlines: committee PowerPoint—fourth week of February 2030; in-person Austin presentation—first week of March 2030; final report—second week of April 2030. Asset/Liability Study assistance is to be determined.

result.title: SECTION THREE - COAERS TERMS AND CONDITIONS
result.summary: The section sets a five-year service term (2026–2030), annual Board performance reviews, qualified staffing and notice of personnel changes, and prior approval for subcontractors; specified obligations survive expiration or termination. It covers termination for breach or convenience, cure and notice periods, payment of eligible costs, return and protection of COAERS information, Texas Public Information Act requests, and COAERS ownership and retention of contract work. The contractor must maintain specified insurance and certificates, report coverage changes, and defend and indemnify COAERS for contractor-related claims, including intellectual-property infringement, but not COAERS’ own negligence. Texas law and Travis County venue apply, without waiver of sovereign immunity; contractor personnel and subcontractors are independent contractors. The section also requires licensing assurances, financial-record retention and access for COAERS audits and the City of Austin actuarial audit, warrants no conflicts or improper gifts or financial interests, addresses required relationship disclosures, and requires compliance with actuarial professional rules.

nodes.title: Contract Terms and Conditions
nodes.summary: The contract terms also apply to subcontractors. The service period runs for five years, January 1, 2026, through December 31, 2030. At least annually, the contractor must send an employee to a Board performance evaluation meeting and, at its own expense, complete a questionnaire beforehand. The contractor must assign qualified personnel; it may substitute equally qualified and skilled key personnel at its reasonable discretion, with written notice to COAERS of proposed changes. COAERS prefers not to use subcontractors, and the contractor must obtain prior written approval from the COAERS Executive Director before a subcontractor provides services. Confidentiality, indemnification, transition, records, actuarial and independent actuarial rights, property rights, dispute resolution, invoice and fee verification, and default provisions survive contract termination or expiration.

nodes.title: 3.5 Termination
key_items: SECTION THREE - COAERS TERMS AND CONDITIONS; 3.1 Contract Period; 3.2 Annual Performance Evaluation; 3.3 Personnel
SECTION THREE - COAERS TERMS AND CONDITIONS
nodes.summary: Either party may terminate for an uncured breach after written notice and a 30-day cure period, or on at least 30 days’ written notice; COAERS may also terminate without cause effective 30 days after notice. Contractor is owed eligible non-cancellable expenses and pro rata payment for services through termination, and must return COAERS information. Contractor must protect COAERS information, including health and legally confidential personal information, while recognizing that records may be subject to the Texas Public Information Act. COAERS will notify Contractor of relevant requests within a reasonable time; Contractor must assist with responses and notify COAERS General Counsel within 24 hours of certain third-party requests. Work produced under the relationship belongs exclusively to COAERS, with rights assigned and assistance provided to perfect them; work must be delivered for retention upon request. Contractor must maintain occurrence-based, primary, non-contributory errors and omissions, general liability, automobile, and workers’ compensation insurance, and provide certificates within 10 business days naming COAERS as additional insured. COAERS insurance is excess and non-contributory.

nodes.title: Confidentiality, Public Records, and Work Product
nodes.summary: The contractor must protect information received from COAERS, including health, personal, and statutorily confidential information. COAERS remains subject to the Texas Public Information Act, will notify the contractor of relevant information requests within a reasonable time, and decides whether to seek an Attorney General ruling; the contractor must assist with responsive documents and notify COAERS General Counsel within 24 hours of third-party requests for state-provided information. The contract and related data may be public. Work produced under the contract belongs exclusively to COAERS upon creation, is treated as work made for hire, and is irrevocably assigned to COAERS if needed. COAERS may secure intellectual-property protections; the contractor must assist without additional charge and provide work for storage and retention upon request.

nodes.title: 3.8 Insurance
nodes.summary: The contractor must maintain occurrence-based, primary, non-contributory errors and omissions, commercial general liability, automobile liability, and workers’ compensation insurance throughout the agreement. Within 10 business days of signing, it must provide certificates naming COAERS as an additional insured; COAERS coverage is excess and non-contributory. The contractor must report policy changes or cancellations within 30 calendar days and use licensed insurers rated “A” by AM Best. It must defend and indemnify COAERS and related parties against claims arising from contractor-side acts or omissions, but not COAERS’ own negligence. Texas law governs, with venue in Travis County. The contract does not waive COAERS’ sovereign immunity or other protections, including through delay or failure to enforce them. The contractor and its personnel and subcontractors are independent contractors, not COAERS employees; COAERS is not liable to subcontractors, and the contractor remains responsible for compliant services. The contractor must also indemnify COAERS against intellectual-property infringement claims; this provision is incomplete in the provided text.

result.title: EXHIBIT F – FIRM QUESTIONNAIRE
result.summary: Exhibit F is a firm questionnaire to be completed in Section 3 by reproducing each heading and question and answering with supporting details. It covers the firm’s history, ownership, corporate form, years in business, Texas licensure, proposed team credentials, Supervising Actuary, other clients and ADC plans, continuity arrangements, and staff turnover. It requests consultancy quality controls, accountability, support tools, working-paper retention, subcontractor use, professional-liability insurance and limits, and liability caps. It addresses technology and disaster recovery, required client systems, confidential-data handling and retention, privacy training, and breach detection and notification. It seeks disclosures of significant media coverage and responses, relevant litigation, arbitration, regulatory sanctions, and staff discipline. The firm must describe ADC valuation experience and its annual COAERS Risk Sharing Valuation Study approach under Texas law and the Funding Approach, including employer contributions, normal cost, gain/loss layers, corridor limits, and responses to required member-rate increases in support of Joint Funding Policy goals. It also covers experience studies, recommended actuarial assumptions, modeling tools, deadline capacity, onboarding tasks and timeline, and the firm’s value proposition.

nodes.title: Ownership, Organization, and Resources
nodes.summary: Exhibit F is a firm questionnaire to be completed in Section 3 of the proposal by retyping each heading and question and providing answers with any needed details. Under Ownership, Organization, and Resources, it requests the firm’s history and development of its actuarial services team, ownership structure and corporate form, years in business, and confirmation of Texas licensure. It also asks for the proposed COAERS team members’ credentials and experience, identification and qualifications of the Supervising Actuary responsible for the work, the team’s other clients and which are actuarially determined contribution plans, arrangements ensuring continuous relationship coverage when primary team members are unavailable, and disclosure and comment on turnover among actuarial personnel assigned or proposed for the COAERS account.

nodes.title: Risk Management – Consultancy
nodes.summary: The text requests proposal information on four areas. Consultancy risk management: internal quality controls and Supervising Actuary accountability; team support and tools; working-paper retention; use and roles of subcontractors or non-employees; engagement insurance carriers, coverage, limits, proof, and rationale for professional-liability limits; and any liability caps and rationale. Technology and confidential-information protection: systems supporting services and disaster recovery; systems COAERS must use; secure receipt, electronic and physical protection, and retention of confidential data; staff privacy training; breach detection and notification processes. Professional reputation: significant media reports from the past year and firm responses; relevant litigation, arbitration, or regulatory sanctions in the past five years; and disciplinary actions involving assigned staff. Risk-sharing valuation studies: experience providing annual ADC valuation information and the proposed annual COAERS Risk Sharing Valuation Study approach, demonstrating knowledge of applicable Texas statutory and funding requirements, including calculating the employer’s required contribution for the upcoming calendar year.

nodes.title: Risk Management, Data Protection, and Reputation
key_items: Risk Management - Technology & Protection of Confidential Information
nodes.summary: The page asks about determining Errors and Omissions insurance coverage and why the firm may limit liability for actuarial services to COAERS. It covers the systems supporting actuarial work and their disaster recovery, systems COAERS must use, how confidential information is received, secured, and retained, staff training on protecting personal information, and procedures for identifying and reporting breaches. It also requests major media reports from the past 12 months concerning client services and any firm responses; business litigation, arbitration, or regulatory sanctions involving actuarial and consulting services over the past five years; and professional disciplinary actions involving assigned team members.

nodes.title: Experience with Risk Sharing Valuation Studies
nodes.summary: Requests information on the firm’s past or current experience providing annual valuation data for other clients’ Actuarially Determined Contributions (ADCs), and its approach to conducting COAERS’s annual Risk Sharing Valuation Study in accordance with Texas Civil Statutes Article 6243n, Section 10(c), and the Funding Approach. The response should explain how the firm will calculate the upcoming calendar year’s Employer Required Contribution, develop plan normal cost and gain/loss layers, and assess the ADC against the City Contribution Corridor’s minimum and maximum. It should also describe how the firm would help COAERS and the City plan actions if the ADC exceeds the corridor maximum and the Member Contribution Rate must rise by more than 2%, while supporting the goals of their Joint Funding Policy.

nodes.title: Experience Studies & Actuarial Assumptions
key_items: Modeling; Capacity to Perform Work & Meet Deliverables; Onboarding
Capacity to Perform Work & Meet Deliverables
nodes.summary: The text requests information about the firm’s experience providing actuarial experience studies and its approach to reviewing and recommending assumptions for inflation, investment returns, post-retirement mortality, plan expenses, individual salary increases, and payroll growth. It asks about modeling capabilities, software and tools for projecting outcomes of future experience or plan changes, and the firm’s capacity to complete the Section 2 scope by its Section 2.10 deadlines. It also requests a detailed onboarding list of tasks, deliverables, and timeline for COAERS, and the firm’s value proposition for actuarial consulting services.

result.title: EXHIBIT G – SCOPE OF SERVICES ACKNOWLEDGEMENT
result.summary: Exhibit G asks the proposer to acknowledge COAERS’ scope and requirements, identify any impediments to performing the work or working with COAERS, and mark each item as agreed to as written or not; disagreements require comments or alternative language. The proposal will be evaluated partly on these responses. Items cover actuarial services: personnel, annual risk-sharing valuation, GASB 67 and 68 reporting, interest-credit recommendations, QEBA allocation, financial-statement assistance, asset/liability studies, experience studies, and service deadlines. Contract and compliance topics include performance evaluation, contract period and termination, surviving terms, confidentiality and open records, applicable law and venue, sovereign immunity, independent-contractor status, intellectual property and infringement, audit rights and document retention, actuarial audits, conflicts and financial interests or gifts, professional standards, work made for hire, indemnification, and insurance.

result.title: EXHIBIT H – COST PROPOSAL
result.summary: Exhibit H requests a cost proposal with a price for each service for each contract year, 2026–2030, based on RFP Section 2. It provides estimated-hours and fixed-price fields for core services: annual actuarial valuation (risk-sharing study), GASB 67 reporting and accounting information, GASB 68 financial reporting information for the City of Austin, QEBA allocation, interest-rate recommendation letter, and financial-statement actuarial assistance, plus 2027 asset/liability study assistance and a 2030 experience study. Bidders must also provide hourly rates, exclusive of travel, for supervising and other actuaries, consultants, support staff, analysts, and other staff. The form invites relevant pricing information, including assumptions, exclusions, and desired payment terms.

result.title: EXHIBIT I – RESPONDENT’S PROPOSAL FORMAT AND REQUIREMENTS
result.summary: Proposals must contain nine clearly labeled parts in the specified order: (1) completed Exhibits A–D, with Exhibit B addressing Texas conflict-of-interest disclosure requirements; respondents must determine whether it applies, as COAERS cannot advise them. (2) Exhibit E identifying the Supervising Actuary, assigned staff resumes, and team organizational chart. (3) Corporate documentation, certificates for errors and omissions, commercial general, automobile, and workers’ compensation insurance, audited 2023 and 2024 financial statements with auditor reports, and Exhibit F questionnaire responses. (4) Completed Exhibit G services-and-requirements chart and clearly stated exceptions or alternatives in Exhibit H; state if there are none. COAERS may reject proposals for exceptions or revisions. (5) Work samples: actuarial valuation, risk-sharing study or similar, experience study, GASB 67 and 68 reports, client communication, and optional others. (6) Exhibit H cost proposal, including estimated hours, plus relevant pricing. (7) Master Services Agreement addressing RFP scope and terms. (8) At least four similar-service client references with project and contact details; COAERS will contact them. (9) Other relevant information demonstrating value.

result.summary: The proposal checklist requires a table of contents with page numbers, trade-secret/confidential material marked, 14-point font on every page, and one electronic original emailed to rfp@coaers.org by 5:00 PM Central on July 30, 2025. Required contents are: Part 1, Exhibits A–D (submission sheet, applicable conflict-of-interest questionnaire, contact information, and trade-secret acknowledgement); Part 2, Exhibit E, staff information identifying the supervising actuary, assigned staff resumes, and organizational chart; Part 3, corporate organization documents, proof of insurance, latest audited financial statements and auditor’s report, and Exhibit F firm questionnaire; Part 4, Exhibit G scope-and-requirements acknowledgement chart and detailed explanations of exceptions; Part 5, work samples; Part 6, Exhibit H cost proposal and hours; Part 7, contract or Master Services Agreement including terms in Sections 2 and 3; Part 8, at least four references; and Part 9, additional respondent information.
